## Interfaces

### interface `audio`

AudioService: headless PCM playback and capture over the virtio-sound device. `beep` queues a tone of the given frequency (Hz) and duration (milliseconds) into the same mixer - the device is reached as a capability (the channel this interface is served on), never as ambient device access. `open-stream` returns a sub-channel served as `pcm-stream`; rates from 8 through 48 kHz and one or two channels are accepted, then converted to the hardware's fixed 48 kHz stereo periods. `open-capture` is the same in reverse: a sub-channel served as `pcm-capture`, converted DOWN from the hardware's 48 kHz stereo to the rate and channel count asked for. It answers not-found on a machine whose sound device has no input stream, which is an ordinary machine rather than an error.  THE DEVICE MODEL (additive at version 1): `devices` is the inventory every scope may read, `open-stream-to` and `open-capture-from` name a device instead of following the default - and move to the default when it leaves - and `open-voice` opens a duplex voice session at 8 or 16 kHz mono on a connection allowed both ways. A stream opened with no device at all is accepted and plays into silence, counted, until one arrives.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `beep` | `beep(freq: u16, millis: u32) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 2 | `open-stream` | `open-stream(rate: u32, channels: u8) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 3 | `open-capture` | `open-capture(rate: u32, channels: u8) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 4 | `devices` | `devices() -> list<audio-device>` |  |
| 5 | `open-stream-to` | `open-stream-to(device: u32, rate: u32, channels: u8) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 6 | `open-capture-from` | `open-capture-from(device: u32, rate: u32, channels: u8) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 7 | `open-voice` | `open-voice(rate: u32) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |

### interface `pcm-stream`

A playback stream returned by `audio.open-stream`. Samples are signed 16-bit little-endian, interleaved by channel; one `write` contains whole sample frames. `write` returns the number of source frames accepted (possibly a prefix) only after bounded playback capacity is available, making synchronous IPC backpressure the playback clock. Closing the channel is equivalent to `close`; explicit close drains accepted samples first.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `write` | `write(data: buffer) -> result<u32, error>` |  |
| 2 | `close` | `close() -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 3 | `latency` | `latency() -> u32` | The stream's latency in microseconds: what it holds queued, and its device's own. |

### interface `pcm-capture`

A capture stream returned by `audio.open-capture`. Samples are signed 16-bit little-endian, interleaved by channel, and one `read` answers exactly one device period converted into the stream's format - a bounded amount, so a recorder that stops asking stops the flow rather than filling a queue nobody drains. A read blocks until the device has filled a period, which makes the device the capture clock the way playback backpressure is the playback clock. An empty answer means the stream is over; closing the channel is equivalent to `close`.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `read` | `read() -> result<list<u8>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `close` | `close() -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 3 | `latency` | `latency() -> u32` | The device's own latency in microseconds. |

### interface `audio-admin`

Privileged launcher boundary that mints factories restricted to one direction. A connection from `open-streams` may only `open-stream`; one from `open-captures` may only `open-capture`. Neither can queue `beep` tones, and NEITHER CAN DO THE OTHER'S JOB: "may record" is not "may make a sound", and a launcher that cannot say which it is granting is a launcher that hands a microphone to anything that beeps.  `open-voices` MINTS THE THIRD: a connection that may only `open-voice` - a duplex session, which records as well as plays and so is granted as neither alone (`audio-voice`).

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `open-streams` | `open-streams() -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `open-captures` | `open-captures() -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |
| 3 | `open-voices` | `open-voices() -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |

### interface `voice-session`

A DUPLEX VOICE SESSION from `audio.open-voice`: mono at the session's rate, signed 16-bit little-endian. `write` is playback with the same backpressure as `pcm-stream`; `read` answers one period of what the voice device - or the default input - heard, converted to the session's rate. OPENING A SESSION IS WHAT BRINGS A HEADSET'S AUDIO LINK UP and closing the last one takes it down.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `write` | `write(data: buffer) -> result<u32, error>` |  |
| 2 | `read` | `read() -> result<list<u8>, error>` |  |
| 3 | `set-call` | `set-call(state: call-state) -> result<unit, error>` | The call this session declares - or none. The voice device is told; with none declared anywhere, a headset is told there is no call and its commands are refused. |
| 4 | `commands` | `commands() -> result<stream<call-command>, error>` | The voice device's call commands as they arrive. |
| 5 | `latency` | `latency() -> u32` | The session's latency both ways, in microseconds. |
| 6 | `close` | `close() -> result<unit, error>` |  |
